jordan: Quick question — who is authoritative for traffic splits vs feature flags at runtime? If product flips a LaunchDarkly flag but the Console has a rollout policy, which one should win? Need clear precedence for canaries/guards.

anne: Short answer: runtime rollout policies (console/API) should be the source of truth for routing decisions. Feature flags live at the app/service layer and can influence behavior, but we need a documented precedence. cc @vikram

vikram: We sketched this in the design sync. Proposal: precedence order = 1) runtime rollout policy (origin=console|api) 2) service-evaluated feature flags (server-side) 3) client-side flags. Runtime policy may include a `force` bit to override lower layers.

maria: How do guards (quota, entitlements, region checks) interact? If runtime routes 10% to v2 but the guard blocks that subset, do we fallback to v1 or return an error? Need deterministic behavior.

vikram: Proposed deterministic behavior: guards are evaluated after routing decision; if a guard denies, we resolve to an explicit fallback variant if provided, otherwise to the primary variant. Suggested schema example: 

```json
{
  "policy": {
    "origin": "console",
    "split": { "v2": 0.1, "v1": 0.9 },
    "guards": ["quota","region"],
    "fallback": "v1",
    "force": true
  }
}
```

This makes behavior predictable and auditable.

jordan: We also need telemetry: capture `effective_source`, `applied_split`, `resolved_by` (guard/fallback) in traces and metrics so teams can debug why a request went to a variant.

anne: Agree. Also add a `shadow` mode for console policies so product can shadow traffic without taking routing authority (useful for experiments).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout created: model-inference v2 -> 10% in us-west1 (run-id 2024-06-05_09:32).

maria: Ok i'll draft an RFC to update the API contract and Console UX with precedence, force/ shadow flags, and telemetry fields. Will include examples + fallback semantics.

jordan: :thumbsup: assigning RFC to @maria and @vikram. Follow-ups: API should accept `origin`, `force` boolean, `fallback` field, and return `effective_source` in the eval response. Let's aim to ship API + Console UI changes before the next canary.

vikram: I'll update the runtime config parsing to prefer `policy.origin` when present and emit a warning if a conflicting service flag is set. Also will add a telemetry tag for `resolved_precedence`.

maria: Thanks — i'll create the RFC PR and ping for review.

jordan: Thanks everyone, this clears up immediate ambiguity. We should capture this in the runbook so on-call knows how to interpret split vs flag conflicts.
